claims.text: A high-throughput method combining ab initio simulations with machine-learning-guided Bayesian optimization can design refractory HEAs that are intrinsically strong, ductile, and low in weight.
The relevant initial material is a disordered refractory high-entropy alloy containing multiple high-melting-point elements and lighter-metal additions.
The proposed computational framework can screen a broad composition space and predict compositions balancing strength, ductility, and density.
The simulations represent high-temperature synthesis and near-equilibrium cooling.
The modeled conditions capture phase formation and microstructural evolution.
The designed alloys form a refined microstructure with optimal short-range order and phase dispersion.
Short-range order and phase dispersion mediate dislocation motion and stress distribution.
The computational framework identifies a balanced ratio of high-melting refractory elements to lighter elements.
Balancing refractory and lighter elements facilitates grain refinement.
Balancing refractory and lighter elements stabilizes beneficial phase mixtures.
Grain refinement and beneficial phase mixtures promote both high strength and ductility.
Adding lighter elements reduces overall alloy density.
Alloys designed with the proposed method will have better mechanical performance than alloys designed using conventional thermo-kinetic simulations alone.
Alloys designed with the proposed method will have lower density than alloys designed using conventional thermo-kinetic simulations alone.
Simulation fidelity, descriptor quality, unmodeled phase transformations, and kinetic effects can limit predictive performance.
Limited machine-learning training data and synthesis-dependent phase evolution may cause simulated microstructures to differ from experimentally realized microstructures.

contradictions.description: The conditions field says phase formation and microstructural evolution are captured by the model, while the boundary and uncertainty fields acknowledge that phase transformations, kinetic factors, and synthesis-dependent phase evolution may not be captured.
